title: U.S. Southwest semiconductor workforce and supplier scaling evidence
question: Can local supplier and workforce systems support semiconductor scaling?
why_it_matters: Funded semiconductor projects only become operating capacity if labor pipelines, construction capacity, suppliers, training systems, and capital commitments can keep up.
current_support: FTFN has national CHIPS context, MAG regional projections, a named TSMC registered technician apprenticeship with an initial eight-person cohort and a later 46-person cohort, a City-relayed July 2026 update saying the first Arizona fab is in volume production, second-fab construction is complete, and TSMC Arizona employs more than 3,500 people, plus BLS May 2025 Phoenix-Mesa-Chandler occupation-group employment and wage estimates.
missing_evidence: apprenticeship completion, credential, retention, and placement outcomes
training capacity relative to fab and supplier demand
facility occupation mix, vacancies, attrition, and hiring demand
candidate_records: MAG 2023 population, housing, and employment projections
TSMC apprenticeship outcome and retention data
Arizona occupation-specific labor and vacancy data
next_action: Move from metropolitan occupation-group context to semiconductor-specific occupations, vacancies, hiring and attrition, apprenticeship completion and retention, construction-trade capacity, and supplier operating records before making workforce or supplier sufficiency claims.
notes: Phase 55I adds a current metropolitan employment and wage baseline after Phase 51C's cohort and employer records. The gap remains unresolved because the BLS record is cross-industry and does not report semiconductor vacancies, hiring, attrition, training outcomes, construction capacity, or supplier-network maturity.
